Wave 5 (main.rs bootstrap): replaced the 27-line scaffold stub with a 498-line real bootstrap following spec Â§15's 32-step main() order-of-operations table (parseArgs->offline-env->bootstrap SettingsManager->version/help gates->resolveAppMode/takeOverStdout->flag validation->migrations->trusted SettingsManager->session-cwd resolution->createSessionManager branch order->--name->ModelRuntime::create->--help/--list-models late-exit->sdk::create_agent_session->initial-message assembly->diagnostics->dispatch to print_mode::run_print_mode). Two new modules: runtime_host.rs (PrintModeSession/AgentSessionRuntimeHost bridge over a real Agent+SessionManager, since sdk.rs never builds AgentSession) and initial_message.rs (buildInitialMessage + text-only @file processing). Found+fixed a real Wave-4 bug while wiring: sdk.rs's stream closure passed an empty env map instead of the real process environment, silently disabling the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fallback; also added --api-key runtime-override plumbing (hazard Â§16.30). Live-verified with no configured credentials: pirust --version -> 0.0.1; --help -> byte-identical help, exit 0; -p "hi" with zero credentials -> "No models available" + exit 1 (correct); with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the full pipeline resolves a model, builds the Agent, runs a real turn, makes a genuine HTTPS request to api.anthropic.com, and persists a byte-plausible session JSONL with the real HTTP 401 body â€” proof the pipeline reaches Anthropic's real servers end-to-end. Wave 6 (live differential+hardening): no real Anthropic credentials existed in this environment, so the differential ran against a local llama-server (llama.cpp, Qwen3.5-0.8B) implementing a genuine Anthropic-Messages-compatible /v1/messages endpoint, reached via the SAME models.json baseUrl-override mechanism already built in Wave 3 (zero new code needed). Real pi was run unmodified from its own TS source (../pi, no dist/ build exists) via a throwaway Node ESM resolve-hook runner using the same alias-mapping pattern the existing oracle scripts already use; ../pi checkout stayed clean throughout (confirmed via git status). Two scenarios (text-mode real bash-tool call; --mode json real write-then-read tool calls) run against both real pi and pirust from the same cwd with --provider anthropic --model <same local model>. RESULT: session JSONL entry types and assistant-message field order are structurally identical between real pi and pirust for both scenarios (values differ only in ids/timestamps/model text, as expected). --mode json event-type vocabulary: found ONE real gap â€” real pi's json stream ends with {"type":"agent_settled"}; pirust's did not. Root cause: print_mode.rs's AgentSessionEvent::AgentSettled variant already existed (Wave 4/5, correctly documented as "emitted once per prompt, after the last agent_end", and required by spec Â§13) but runtime_host.rs's SingleTurnSession (the AgentSession-substitute bridge) never constructed one â€” to_session_event is a pure 1:1 AgentEvent->AgentSessionEvent map and AgentSettled has no AgentEvent counterpart to map from; it must be synthesized. FIX: SingleTurnSession now stores the subscribe()-registered listener and prompt() invokes it once more with AgentSettled after wait_for_idle() (this wave's sequential prompt() calls have no queue/retry machinery of their own, so idle always means settled). Re-verified: print_mode_golden.rs still 10/10 green, and a fresh live run's json-event-type set-diff against real pi's is now EMPTY in both directions for the write/read scenario. entry_appended (the other spec-Â§13-named event) legitimately stays deferred (needs a loaded extension, feat-007) â€” confirmed absent from BOTH real pi's and pirust's output in these non-extension scenarios, not assumed. SELF-REFERENTIALITY AUDIT: the agent_settled gap above IS the audit's finding â€” Wave 4/5's type-level modeling was correct but its runtime wiring was never exercised against a real end-to-end run, so a real gap shipped silently under "10/10 golden"; sdk_canned_turn.rs separately confirmed as correctly-scoped internal-wiring test (Faux provider, not claiming Pi byte-compat); system_prompt_golden.rs/provider_attribution_golden.rs confirmed still oracle-generated. TIMING (release build, existing [profile.release] lto+strip; no hyperfine installed, used PowerShell Measure-Command, 10 runs each): pirust --version/--help steady-state ~8-10ms, in the earlier-reported jcode near-native floor (10.1-19.3ms). Real pi via the unbundled Node resolve-hook runner: ~2.1-2.7s â€” NOT a fair comparison to a properly bundled dist/cli.js (none exists in this checkout); flagged as a residual, not a blocker. MEMORY: pirust's release binary (127KB on disk) exits too fast (~8-10ms) to sample a meaningful idle working set; real pi under Node sampled ~125.7MB working set mid-run â€” a rough first data point, not a rigorous benchmark. 508+ workspace tests green (up from ~477 pre-Wave-4), fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, ./init.sh green with no oracle drift after the Wave 6 fix. NAMED DEFERRALS (documented, not silent, all correctly out of feat-005's own scope): blockImages message filtering (sdk.ts:250-285); session restore (is_continuing always false â€” session.rs's job); onPayload/onResponse extension hooks (no slot on pirust_ai::StreamOptions yet, feat-007's job); settings-validation-error fallback (defaults silently inside the stream wrapper rather than surfacing, deferred); project trust hard-codes untrusted-unless-approve (stricter than Pi, the safe direction); message-level not event-level session persistence; NoSignals used so SIGTERM/SIGHUP fall back to OS-default terminate instead of Pi's graceful dispose-then-exit; RPC mode (feat-012), interactive TUI+extensions+resource-loader (feat-006/007), non-anthropic providers (feat-008), package-manager verbs/HTML export/telemetry/self-update/proxy (not ported at all, per spec Â§18). A real apples-to-apples pirust-vs-pi timing/memory comparison against a properly built pi dist and real Anthropic credentials remains open for whenever both are available â€” named as a residual, not a blocker, since it was never part of this feature's own ACCEPTANCE line.

features.description: REVISED: real Pi renamed packages/orchestrator to packages/server (commit 8495f9d0d) and redesigned it - the old process-spawning/Radius/IPC-socket design (supervisor.ts, radius.ts, rpc-process.ts, storage.ts, cli.ts) no longer exists in pi_space/pi. Current scope: port @earendil-works/pi-server + @earendil-works/pi-protocol as a transport-neutral, multi-session-multiplexing server library - binary CBOR-over-length-prefixed-frames wire protocol (TypeBox-schema-validated), a PiServer connection/handshake state machine, a reference-counted LiveSessionManager (attach/detach/dispose lifecycle), a revision-numbered ServerSnapshotPublisher, and a Unix-socket PiServerListener transport. Nothing in pi_space/pi (incl. packages/coding-agent) currently implements PiServerService, so wiring one to pirust-agent-core's AgentHarness is a pirust-side addition (named, not silently invented), not a port - only the library itself (protocol codec + server + sessions + snapshots + unix transport) is oracle-verified against Pi's own conformance test suite.
